This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER
This is first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of bail, pending the trial.

The applicant has been arrested on 07.11.2022 in connection with S.T.No.105/2017 pending before the Additional Sessions Judge, Shahdol, which has arisen out of complaint case filed before the JMFC for offence punishable under Section 363, 120B, 366A, 373, 372, 376 and 506B of IPC.

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, prosecutrix filed a complaint before the JMFC Burhar alleging that on 08.12.2009, she along with her husband had gone for wages.
Her 16 years old daughter was at home.
At around 6:00 P.M., she returned to home but left for Burhar vegetable market for purchasing vegetables.

In the meantime, Gopal Singh, Santosh Singh, Betu Vishkarma, Durga Lal,
Prahlad Kanchi and Baba Vishkarma were waiting and thereafter they forcibly kidnapped her daughter and took her to Satna.
In Satna Gopal Singh and Santosh Singh raped her and that time rest of the accused were standing outside as watchmen.
Thereafter, they sold out her daughter for a consideration of Rs.10.00 lac to Mukesh Kanjar who later repeatedly committed rape with her daughter.
When Police did not take any action, complaint was filed and on the basis of statement under Section 200 and 202 of Cr.P.C complaint was registered.
In due course matter was committed to the Court of Session for trial.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
He never kidnapped and raped prosecutrix's daughter..
He has enmity with the prosecutrix over the dispute between the children of Mohalla.
Prosecutrix and her daughter are in habit of making false complaints against innocent persons and realizing money by retracting their evidence before the trial Court.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant be released on bail pending the trial.
O n the other hand, learned counsel for the objector as well as learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant.
Applicant is in jail for more than 3 months.
Therefore, having taken into consideration the entirety of the facts, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre trial detention of the applicant is not warranted.
Consequently, this first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

It is directed that applicant - Anil @ Betu be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Jasleen Anil @ Betu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119027257/
